headline: Kai, fresh Houthi fire kept Riyadh's airport shut through Sunday, and futures still point higher into bank earnings and CPI week.
subline: Brent holds near $103, JPMorgan opens earnings season Tuesday, and Wednesday's CPI decides whether the Fed gets to pause.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:40 AM ET · index values are futures; bond market closed for Columbus Day · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Futures rise with the big banks on deck Tuesday
items.sentence: S&P futures are up 0.25 percent early Monday as JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs and Citi open third-quarter earnings season Tuesday, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: CPI Wednesday; markets lean December for the next hike
items.sentence: September CPI lands Wednesday as the week's main event, with Polymarket pricing a 16.5 percent chance of a hike on October 28 but 74.5 percent for a quarter point by December, per The Rio Times.

items.title: Bond market closed today; ten-year at 24-year high
items.sentence: Stocks trade normal hours but SIFMA closed dollar fixed income for Columbus Day, freezing the ten-year at last week's 24-year highs until Tuesday, per Investing Live.

items.title: Oil eases on the energy truce; diesel does not
items.sentence: WTI slipped toward $91 after Trump's claimed Russia-Ukraine energy truce, while U.S. diesel averages $6.28 a gallon against $3.68 a year ago, per Yahoo Finance and CBS News.

items.title: Bitcoin steadies near $83,500 after a bruising week
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades near $83,500 this morning, up 0.66 percent, per Yahoo Finance. The week behind it was a 3.3 percent slide driven by roughly $730 million in spot-ETF outflows and over $1.1 billion in liquidations before shorts began covering, per The Crypto Times.

items.title: New strikes keep Riyadh's airport closed; flights suspended
items.sentence: Saturday's strike on King Khalid International killed at least 12 and wounded 309, and another projectile closed the airport Sunday as Lufthansa, Emirates and others suspended Riyadh flights, per CBS News.

items.title: Iran calls U.S. response 'insufficient' as talks stall
items.sentence: Tehran's top security official said Iran is no longer responding to Washington and threatened regional 'cables, data centers, AI facilities' if intense fighting resumes, per CBS News.

items.title: Kyiv says Russia already violated the energy truce
items.sentence: A day after Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire, Zelenskyy said Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities have not stopped, per NBC News.

items.title: Gulf tanker attacks hit wartime highs around Hormuz
items.sentence: Attacks on shipping have surged to wartime highs as Iran tries to choke off Gulf oil exports, with the IRGC blaming a mine for the latest tanker explosion, per CNBC.

items.title: Murphy warns the war is 'spiraling out of control'
items.sentence: With midterms three weeks out, Sen. Chris Murphy said the U.S. should not retaliate on Saudi Arabia's behalf, per CBS News.

items.title: Microsoft's leaders ask Washington to regulate AI now
items.sentence: Brad Smith said a washing machine faces more safety rules than AI as he, Nadella and Gates pushed for pre-launch reviews and emergency kill switches, per Benzinga.

items.title: Amazon circles Decart at a reported $7 billion
items.sentence: Amazon is reportedly in talks to buy the Israeli world-model startup after Anthropic agreed to roughly the same price and then walked away following diligence, per Startup Fortune.

items.title: TSMC expected to post a sixth straight record profit
items.sentence: TSMC reports Thursday and ASML Wednesday in the week's main test of AI-chip demand, with TSMC seen posting a sixth consecutive record quarterly profit, per Reuters.

items.title: Apple's smart-home event lands Tuesday in New York
items.sentence: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event is expected to show a touchscreen home hub plus refreshed HomePod mini and Apple TV hardware, per Stocktwits on Yahoo Finance.

items.title: An OpenAI revenue surprise dented chips last week
items.sentence: Thursday's tech selloff followed a report that OpenAI's annualized revenue runs about $20 billion below earlier estimates, and the SOXX chip ETF still ended the week down 5.1 percent, per TheStreet and Stocktwits.
